newsitem.title: THAILAND: THAI OIL FIRM PTT TO SPEED UP PRIVATISATION PLAN.
newsitem.headline: THAI OIL FIRM PTT TO SPEED UP PRIVATISATION PLAN.

text.p: The state-run Petroleum Authority of Thailand (PTT) will speed up privatisation plans to raise around 75 billion baht for government coffers by early next year, a senior PTT official said on Wednesday.
The privatisation project was originally scheduled for the second half of 1998. PTT is valued by analysts at between 250-350 billion baht.

"The privatisation plan is expected to be ready by next month. Once the government approves the proposal, we hope to be able to execute the plan within six months," said the official who asked not to be identified.
"And if we could, we will sell parts of the stake to foreign investors," the official said.
Thailand's severe economic problems have nudged the government into speeding up privatisation of state enterprises to raise funds to bridge the fiscal deficit.
The move was seen as crucial after the government pledged to balance its budget as a condition for access to IMF financial support to revive its troubled economy.

Analysts estimate that the government would be able to raise between 100-250 billion baht from selling parts of its seven major state enterprises whose combined assets totalled nearly one trillion baht.

These agencies include the Electricity Generating Authority of Thailand, the Petroleum Authority of Thailand, the Telephone Organisation of Thailand, Thai Airways International, the Provincial Electricity Authority, the Metropolitan Electricity Authority and the Communications Authority of Thailand.
The PTT official said the agency's financial advisers were finalising the proposal. Among its foreign advisers were Merrill Lynch, CS First Boston, Morgan Stanley and Lehman Brothers.
